h1: The 5 Best Roku Projectors of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 projectors with Roku TV built in, scored on streaming setup, portability, power options and resolution, from $50 to $200.
summary: The Aurzen Roku TV D1R is the Roku projector to buy first: a portable, outdoor-ready unit with Roku's home screen built in. The D1R Cube is the compact variant billed as the first Roku TV smart projector, and the D1R air adds USB-C PD power for flexible use. The Boldever is the 1080p mini pick, and the Miroir is the desktop-friendly budget option.
intro: Roku inside a projector solves the most annoying part of owning one: the streaming stick that has to be plugged in, powered and paired every time you set it up. With Roku TV built in, you power on, sign in and the same home screen you know from a television appears on the wall. That is a real convenience, and it is the reason this short category exists.

The tradeoff is that almost none of the listings state brightness or contrast figures, so Primea editors ranked these five on what they do document: the Roku integration, portability, power options and resolution. Every model needs a Roku account and an internet connection, and all five fall between $50 and $200.

products.name: Aurzen Roku TV D1R Smart Portable Outdoor Projector
products.verdict: The core D1R, with Roku TV, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and a portable, outdoor-ready body.
products.description:
The D1R is the standard model in Aurzen's Roku line: a portable projector with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth that runs Roku's fast home screen and its streaming apps. It requires a Roku account and an internet connection.

It ranks first because it is the model the other D1R variants build on, and its listing gives the clearest description of what you get. The Cube trades shape for the same software, while the air focuses on power.

A fine pick for a backyard movie night or a bedroom wall. The caveat is brightness: the listing states no lumen figure, so use it in dim conditions.
products.idealFor: Movie nights indoors or out for people who already use Roku.
products.skipIf: You need a bright projector for a lit room.

products.name: Aurzen Roku TV D1R Cube Smart Outdoor Projector
products.verdict: A cube-shaped Roku TV projector billed as the world's first.
products.description:
The D1R Cube is billed as the world's first Roku TV smart projector, with a simple, fast home screen and Wi-Fi plus Bluetooth. A cube body is easy to pack and to place on a shelf.

It ranks second because it offers the same Roku experience as the D1R in a more compact shape, but the listing does not describe any performance difference. Choose it when shape and portability are the priority.

It suits travelers and small-room users. The caveat is that, like the D1R, it publishes no brightness or contrast, so judge it as a dim-room device.
cons: Similar to the D1R in features
products.idealFor: Travelers and small rooms that want a cube-sized projector.
products.skipIf: You need a stated lumen rating.

products.name: Aurzen Roku TV D1R air USB-C Powered Portable Projector
products.verdict: USB-C PD power makes it flexible for indoor and outdoor use.
products.description:
The D1R air is a portable Roku TV smart projector with USB-C PD power for flexible indoor and outdoor use. USB-C PD means a power bank or a laptop charger can run it, which cuts the need for a wall outlet.

It ranks third because it is more of a mobile accessory than a home theater, and the listing gives no picture details beyond the power feature. Against the standard D1R, the power flexibility is its single advantage.

Choose it for camping, backyard use and anywhere without an outlet. The caveat is that run time depends on the power bank you attach, which the listing does not specify.
cons: Run time depends on your bank
products.idealFor: Camping and backyard movie nights without an outlet.
products.skipIf: You will always have a wall outlet nearby.

products.name: Boldever Roku TV 1080P FHD Mini Smart Projector
products.verdict: A 1080p FHD mini projector with official Roku TV built in.
products.description:
Boldever sells a 1080p FHD mini projector with official Roku TV built in, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, and a simple Roku home screen. It is the one in this group that states a native resolution.

It ranks fourth because the Aurzen models have a clearer portable and outdoor pitch, while the Boldever is a straightforward mini projector. Stating 1080p gives you a reliable sharpness expectation.

Choose it for a bedroom or dorm. The caveat is that the brand is less established than Aurzen, so check the support terms on the product page.
products.idealFor: Bedrooms and dorms that want a stated 1080p picture.
products.skipIf: You want a portable outdoor-focused body.

products.name: Miroir Roku TV Smart Projector with WiFi and Bluetooth
products.verdict: The lowest-priced Roku TV projector here, suited to desktop placement.
products.description:
The Miroir is a Roku TV smart projector with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, noted as better suited for desktop placement. It is the cheapest in the group, in the $50 to $100 bucket on this listing.

It ranks last because the listing carries almost no specifications: no resolution, brightness or portability claims. Its place is as an entry-level way to get Roku on the wall.

A fit for a desk or shelf projection. The caveat is that desktop placement means a fixed spot and a short throw, so plan the layout before buying.
products.idealFor: A first Roku projector on a desk or shelf.
products.skipIf: You want documented resolution or brightness.

whatMatters.detail: Built-in Roku means the projector runs Roku's home screen and apps itself, so you need no streaming stick. It requires a Roku account and an internet connection. Check that the listing says official Roku TV, as the Boldever does, because some units only support casting, which means you still depend on a phone or a separate stick for apps.

Native resolution is the number of real pixels the projector draws. A stated 1080p, as on the Boldever, sets a clear sharpness baseline. Check the listing for native, not supported, because a projector that merely accepts 4K input is often still 720p or 1080p inside, and text looks soft at larger screen sizes.

Brightness decides how well the image survives ambient light. None of these listings gives a lumen figure, so assume dim-room use. Check the product page for ANSI lumens, and prefer a dark room, because a washed-out image defeats the point of a big screen, and a lamp left on in the room cancels most of the contrast.

Wall power gives steady brightness, while USB-C PD, as on the D1R air, lets you run from a power bank. Check the wattage the projector needs and the bank's output, since an underpowered bank leads to dimming or shutdowns during a movie.

Throw distance determines how big the image is at a given distance. A desktop-oriented unit like the Miroir is meant for short distances. Check the listing for throw ratio or screen size range, and measure the distance from the projector to your wall before ordering, since a short-throw mismatch cannot be fixed with software alone.

faq.q: Do Roku projectors need a separate streaming stick?
faq.a: No. The Aurzen D1R, Cube and air and the Boldever have Roku TV built in. You still need a Roku account and an internet connection, and the listings say so.

faq.q: What is the common mistake with Roku projectors?
faq.a: Expecting daylight performance. None of these listings states brightness, so treat them as dim-room units. Wait until evening for the D1R outdoors, and close curtains indoors.

faq.q: Is the Aurzen worth it over the Miroir?
faq.a: If you want a portable, outdoor-ready body, yes. The Aurzen D1R costs $100 to $200 and has a clearer description than the Miroir at $50 to $100, which is listed as desktop-suited.

Use Bluetooth, which all five models list, to pair a speaker or soundbar. The Boldever and Aurzen units support Bluetooth, but check for audio delay on movies, since some speakers lag the picture slightly.

faq.q: How do I keep a projector lens clean?
faq.a: Use a blower and a microfiber cloth, and cap the lens when stored. The D1R Cube is easy to pack, so protect it in a pouch. Never wipe a dusty lens dry.

faq.q: Can I run the D1R air on a power bank?
faq.a: Yes, it uses USB-C PD power. Pick a bank with a PD output that meets the projector's requirement, which its listing does not state, and expect run time to depend on the bank's capacity and on how bright you run the lamp.

finalTake: The Aurzen Roku TV D1R is the Roku projector to buy for most people, because it combines built-in Roku with a portable, outdoor-ready body. The Cube is the better choice for packing, and the D1R air is the one for power banks. The Boldever offers a stated 1080p resolution, and the Miroir is the budget desk option.
